thread:
Sophie L: quick RFC follow-up — thinking about adding cross-tenant cost throttling into the routing decision layer. we've seen noisy tenants (long prompts + large batches) pushing others into fallback small-models. proposal: surface a short-lived tenant 'budget' signal from admission control into the policy eval, and let policies apply temporary penalties before invoking full throttling. want feedback on interface shape and compat risks.

Raj P: can you sketch the proto of the signal? is this a boolean, a score, or a categorical tag? also worried about coupling routing & billing code.

Sophie L: good q. thinking a float score 0..1 called tenant_budget_util where 1.0 means exhausted. policy eval would see it as an additional feature. minimal shape: `{tenant_budget_util: 0.73, window_secs: 60}`. policies can map it to a penalty weight.

Amanda: +1 for a score, not boolean. We should also include an enforcement hint: `soft`, `hard`. soft = routing demotion only, hard = admission rejects. that way downstream admission control can still take stronger action.

Derek: operational concern — we already have policy cache keyed by route/model + tenant. this score is high-cardinality/time-variant. can't put it into the cache key or cache hit rate collapses. we should treat it as an ephemeral signal excluded from cache keys and evaluated after a cached decision is fetched (i.e., decision post-processing).

Jules: that implies two-step decision flow: 1) cached policy -> 2) apply ephemeral penalties. Are we ok with that latency/complexity tradeoff?

Raj P: functionally yes. Implementation-wise we need a deterministic, composable transformation so all runtimes (hosted, dedicated, private) apply the same penalty math. propose a tiny library: `penalty.apply(policy_decision, ephemeral_signals) -> adjusted_decision`. keep it purely arithmetic (no new rules engine).

Sophie L: exactly. we want to avoid a policy language change. small shim arithmetic rules: multiply weight by (1 + alpha * tenant_budget_util). alpha is tunable per-tenant tier. default alpha=2.

Amanda: what about telemetry? need to emit both raw tenant_budget_util and adjusted_weight so we can debug mispenalization. also expose a histogram of adjusted latency and fallback rates per-tenant.

infra-bot: deploy check: canary tag required for runtime change. add `ephemeral-signal` flag to route config.

Derek: rollout plan idea: 1) API + telemetry only (no effect). 2) Add read-only `penalty.apply` wiring behind an opt-in flag. 3) Canary on a few low-risk tenants, monitor fallback rate and p99 latency. 4) global opt-in and then tune alpha.

Sophie L: compatibility: policy archives (old compiled policy blobs) should be unaffected. penalty.apply must accept older decision shapes and be a no-op if not present. also we should version the signal field name (e.g., `ephemeral_v1`).

Raj P: edge-case: what if two ephemeral signals (budget + burst_detected + region_congestion) exist? propose the shim takes a list of bags and applies them in deterministic order. score composition = clamp(sum(weighted_scores), 0, max_penalty). keep simple additive composition.

Amanda: for observability add tags: `signal_budget`, `signal_burst`, `signal_region`. each produces a per-call vector so we can slice in dashboards.

Jules: question on fairness — will this let big customers game the system by splitting requests across tenants? it's an arms race. but we can mitigate by aggregating by billing account and not just tenant id. add `account_id` to signal proto.

Derek: ops note: admission control already knows billing account. routing layer must trust it but validate signature of the signal token to avoid spoofing. we should pass signal via signed header from admission to routing. private deployments: we need a config toggle to disable signing check for air-gapped setups (documented risk).

Sophie L: agreed on signed header & account aggregation. security will draft the HMAC flow.

Raj P: small nit on policy authors: document examples in the policy cookbook. e.g., `when tenant_budget_util > 0.9 then increase cost_penalty by 1.5x` but implemented as arithmetic in shim. keep policy grammar unchanged.

Amanda: test matrix: unit tests for shim math, integration test for caching (ensure no cache bloat), canary dashboard, and a regression test where bogus signals are rejected.

infra-bot: note created: INFRA-7734 "ephemeral tenant signals: routing penalty shim" assigned to @Derek.

Sophie L: next steps: I'll write a short RFC patch with the signal proto, shim math, and rollout plan. ping me if you want to be a reviewer. thanks all :rocket:

Raj P: +1, will review.

Derek: I'll prep the canary dashboard templates and the HMAC spec.

Amanda: happy to add cookbook examples and telemetry panels.

Jules: flagging potential follow-up: evaluate how this interacts with prefetch/cache priming. might need a separate signal for prefetch budget.

Sophie L: noted. we'll track in the RFC.
